question: What questions should I ask a flooring contractor before hiring?
title: Questions to Ask a Flooring Contractor Before Hiring
h1: What Should You Ask a Flooring Contractor Before You Hire One?
description: Before hiring a Sarasota flooring contractor, ask for a written itemized quote, proof of insurance, and how they test slab moisture, per ASTM F2170.
capsule: Before hiring a flooring contractor in Sarasota or Manatee County, ask for a written itemized quote covering material, labor, removal and prep, proof of general liability insurance and workers' compensation, and how they test slab moisture. ASTM F2170 caps in-slab relative humidity at 75% before flooring goes down unless the manufacturer allows a higher reading.

sections.h2: What Should You Ask Before Hiring a Flooring Contractor?
sections.html:
Four things matter more than anything else on the sales pitch: how the quote is written, whether the business is properly insured, whether they test the slab before quoting wood or vinyl, and what the warranty actually covers. Everything else, showroom samples, financing offers, install dates, matters less if those four aren't solid.

If you're comparing flooring installers near me results, most of them will look similar on the surface: a phone number, some photos, a service area map. These questions are how you tell the difference before you've signed anything, and a contractor who answers them clearly on the first call is usually worth moving forward with.

Ask for the quote in writing, itemized by material, labor, prep, subfloor repairs, disposal and furniture moving, not one bundled total. A written breakdown is the only way to know what you're actually paying for and to compare it against another bid. We write every quote this way, with material, labor, removal, prep and trim on separate lines, and answer within 24 hours of an in-home estimate. If a contractor resists putting numbers in writing or won't explain a line item when asked, treat that as useful information rather than pushing past it.

See our full breakdown of what causes two quotes for the same room to look different in why flooring quotes vary.

Ask whether the business is actively registered with the state and carries general liability insurance and workers' compensation, or a valid exemption. Florida no longer issues a state license for flooring or tile installation, so "licensed" isn't a claim any honest flooring installer in this state should make; registration and insurance are what you're actually checking for. Ask us for our certificate of insurance and we'll send it before the job starts.

This question matters more than it sounds like it should. A contractor without insurance who damages a wall, breaks a pipe under a slab, or has a worker injured on your property can leave you holding that liability instead of them.

If your home is on a concrete slab, which most Sarasota-area homes are, ask how the contractor tests moisture before recommending wood or vinyl. The industry standard, ASTM F2170, requires in-slab relative humidity to stay at or below 75% unless the flooring or adhesive manufacturer specifies a different limit, with probes set at 40% of slab depth on slabs drying from one side. A contractor who skips this step and quotes wood flooring sight unseen is guessing, and a bad guess on a slab reading is exactly what causes cupping and buckling a year or two after install.

Ask what's covered in writing, for how long, and who actually shows up to do the work. We back every install with a two-year written workmanship warranty and have the owner supervise every job rather than handing it to a subcontracted crew, so ask any contractor you're considering the same thing: who's actually on the floor. Also ask about turnaround: how soon they can start, and roughly how long your specific square footage will take. A vague answer to a timeline question is often a sign the contractor hasn't actually scheduled real crews yet, just penciled you in somewhere.

faqs.q: Do flooring installers in Florida need a state license?
faqs.a: No. Florida issues no state license for flooring or tile installers, and local occupational licensing of the trade was preempted statewide effective July 1, 2024. Business registration and insurance are what you should verify instead.

faqs.q: How much deposit is reasonable to pay upfront?
faqs.a: Industry guidance puts typical contractor deposits at 10-25% of the job, tied to milestones rather than paid in full before work starts. See our full deposit breakdown for specifics.

faqs.q: What's the difference between an estimate and a quote?
faqs.a: An estimate is a rough range before the contractor has measured or tested your slab; a quote is a firm, written number after an in-home visit. We provide free in-home estimates that convert to a written quote once we've measured and tested.
